transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m only sitting in this chair because... look, everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. My wife, the people around me, they just roll their eyes or tell me I'm stressed. But I know what's happening. I'm a fabricator, okay? I work with my hands for a living, forty hours a week down at the plant, so when I come home, I like things a certain way. I know exactly where my things are. But her relative—my wife’s relative—he’s been coming into this house just to get at me. I know he is. 

I mean, my tools don’t just move themselves! I’ll leave my good torque wrench and my calipers right on the center of the workbench, wiped down and everything, and the next morning? They’re kicked under the air compressor or shoved behind the bandsaw. Tools don't grow legs. I know what I put where. And it’s not just the garage, it’s... it’s my downtime, too. My fishing plans. Every single weekend, my plans get spoiled, and it's not by accident. I’ll have the tackle box packed, the rods all rigged up and ready by the door, and suddenly the latch on my good cooler is busted, or the truck battery is mysteriously dead, or my line is tangled to hell. Every weekend! You can't tell me that's just a coincidence or bad luck. 

It’s been going on for months and months now. At first I thought I was just misplacing things, but then you put it all together and... well, I can see it plain as day. He’s trying to take over my place. He’s messing with my stuff, trying to make me look like I'm losing my grip, just trying to push me out of my own home so he can slide right in. And nobody wants to listen to me about it, they just act like I'm making it up, but I know what I'm seeing.
Have you ever seen this person, your wife's relative, in your home when you know he shouldn't be there?

Well, see, that’s... that’s exactly the trap everyone tries to catch me in. My wife says the exact same thing. "Did you actually see him, did you catch him in the act?" No, I haven't looked him dead in the eye standing in my kitchen, but I mean, come on, I don't need to! The guy isn't an idiot. He’s a snake, but he’s not stupid. He knows my schedule inside and out. 

I’ve been at the plant for, what, nineteen years now? Nineteen years on the floor, same exact shift. I punch in at 6:30 AM sharp. Which means I’m pulling out of my driveway by 5:45, maybe 5:50 at the latest if I have to scrape frost off the windshield. He knows that. The whole family knows my routine. So he’s not going to just waltz through the front door while I’m sitting in my recliner, is he? He waits. He bides his time until my truck is gone, and he waits until my wife is out running her errands. She goes to the grocery store over on Route 9 on Tuesdays and Thursdays, usually around 10 AM, and she takes her sweet time chatting with everybody in the aisles, let me tell you. 

That gives him a solid two, maybe three-hour window to just... slip right in. He probably comes through the side gate. The latch on that gate has been tricky since a storm we had last spring—you have to sort of lift the door and push the pin at the same time—but he’s been around the house enough in the past to know the trick to it. 

So, no, I haven't caught him red-handed. I haven't walked into the garage and found him standing there holding my calipers. But you don't need to see the wind to know it's blowing, do you? You see the trees moving. I come home, I check the garage, I look at my workbench, and I can just tell. I can feel that someone’s been in my space, breathing my air, putting their hands on my livelihood. You don't need a photograph of the guy when the proof is sitting right there in front of you every single week.
Have you ever heard your wife's relative in your home when you know you're alone?

Hear him? No, no, I don't hear him stomping around or whispering or anything like that when I'm sitting there by myself. Like I was just explaining, he’s not going to risk that. He knows better. And honestly, if he tried to pull his little stunts while I was actually in the house, I’d hear him coming a mile away. It’s an older split-level, built back in '78, and let me tell you, every single floorboard in that place has a mind of its own. Especially right there in the hallway between the kitchen and the main bathroom. If you step right on the seam where the carpet meets the linoleum, it lets out this loud groan. You can hear it all the way down in the basement. 

Plus, the front door drags. The weather stripping on the bottom is coming loose—I keep meaning to tack it back down, but you know how it is, you work with your hands all week and the last thing you want to do on a Sunday is fix your own door—so it scrapes on the threshold every time you open it. 

So, no, when I'm home alone, it's just quiet. It's just me and the hum of the refrigerator, maybe the baseboard heaters ticking when they kick on. I don't hear him because he makes damn sure not to be there when I am. That’s the whole point everybody seems to be missing. He’s a snake, but he’s careful. He waits until the driveway is empty and the house is dead silent. If I ever actually heard him in the house with me, believe me, I’d march right out there and put a stop to this whole thing right then and there. I wouldn't just sit there listening to him mess with my life. But he doesn't give me the chance. He just waits until I'm gone.
Do you think your wife's relative is trying to harm you directly, or is it more about taking over your place in the home?

Harm me? Like, physically come at me with a pipe or a baseball bat? No, no, he doesn't have the spine for that. That’s not his style at all. He's a sneak. It’s exactly what I’ve been trying to tell everyone, and honestly, it's the whole reason I'm here. I’m only sitting in this office because everybody keeps acting like I’m just imagining it! My wife, her family, the guys down at the plant... they just roll their eyes or tell me I need to relax. But I know what I know. I know my wife’s relative came into this house specifically to get at me. 

It's entirely about taking over my place. I mean, think about the facts here. My tools don’t just move themselves! You don't just accidentally kick a heavy-duty torque wrench under an air compressor, or misplace calipers that have had a dedicated spot on the pegboard for a decade. And my downtime? My fishing plans? Every single weekend, without fail, they get spoiled. You don't get a busted cooler latch and a mysteriously dead truck battery by accident every weekend. It's a calculated move to break my spirit. 

You look at all of this, and after all these months—and it's been going on for months now, day in and day out, just this constant chipping away at my sanity—I can see it plain as day. He’s trying to wear me down. He wants to make me look unreliable, or like I'm losing my mind to my wife, just so he can take over my place. He wants to push me out of my own home, step right into my shoes, and take over everything I've built. It’s a slow push, doc. He wants my life, he wants my spot in that house, and it just drives me up the wall that nobody else will just look at the evidence right in front of their faces!
Do you think it's possible that your wife's relative is not actually doing these things to you?

Doc, I just... did you not hear everything I just laid out for you? Is it possible? No. No, it is absolutely not possible. See, this right here, this is exactly what I'm talking about. I am only sitting here in this office because everybody keeps acting like I am just imagining it. They treat me like I'm making up stories in my head, but I know what I know. I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. 

I mean, let's just look at the basic physics of the situation, alright? My tools do not move themselves. I have been an assembler for nineteen years, I work with tight tolerances, I am a meticulous man. I wipe down my wrenches, I hang them on the pegboard, I even traced the outlines in black marker so I know exactly where every single piece goes. A heavy piece of steel does not just jump off the wall and hide itself under an air compressor. 

And my weekends? You really think my fishing plans get spoiled by accident every single weekend? Every single one? One week the cooler latch is snapped clean off, the next week the truck battery is mysteriously dead as a doornail even though the alternator is perfectly fine, the week after that my good tackle is just gone... you don't get that kind of bad luck by accident. Not week after week. 

It is a deliberate campaign against me. After all these months of this happening, after watching the pattern day in and day out, I can see it plain as day. He has been trying to take over my place and push me out. So no, doc, it is not possible that I'm wrong about this. The only thing that's impossible is how nobody else seems to see what's happening right under their noses.
Have you ever thought someone was out to get you before your wife's relative started doing these things?

Before him? No. No, absolutely not. I see what you're trying to do there, doc. You're trying to figure out if I'm just one of those guys who walks around thinking the sky is falling, or like... like the mailman is reading my letters, or the guys at the plant are conspiring against me. But that is not me. Not even close. 

I mean, look at my track record. I’ve been at the plant for nineteen years. You don’t survive nineteen years on an assembly line if you’re the kind of guy who thinks everybody is out to get you. You just don't. You have to work as a team. I go in, I punch my card, I do my job—and like I told you, I work with tight tolerances, it takes focus, you can't be distracted by imaginary drama—and then I go home. I get along fine with the guys. Sure, maybe Dave over in receiving gets on my nerves when he leaves the forklift uncharged at the end of first shift, but I don't think he's doing it *to* me. He's just lazy, you know? That's just regular life. 

Even before we bought the split-level, back when we rented that little duplex over on Miller Road, I never had a single issue with anybody. The neighbors and I, we'd wave, maybe I'd help them shovel their drive in the winter if I already had the snowblower out, but we just minded our own business. I’ve always minded my own business. 

So, no. I have never felt like somebody was after me before this. That’s what makes this whole situation so damn frustrating! I didn't ask for this. I was perfectly happy just working my forty hours, keeping my tools organized, and taking my boat out on Saturdays. I’ve never had an enemy in my life. This isn't some... some pattern with me, or me just making things up. It is specifically him, and it only started when he decided he wanted what I have.
Do you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that you might be mistaken about your wife's relative being behind these events?

Doc, are we... are we going in circles here? Because I feel like I'm a broken record, and I don't know how many different ways I can explain this to you. Did you not write down what I said two minutes ago? You're asking me again if there's a 'small possibility' I'm mistaken, and the answer is still exactly the same. No. Zero. Not a fraction of a percent. 

Look, I’m only here, sitting in this chair, wasting a perfectly good Tuesday afternoon, because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. My wife, her family, the guys at work, and now you, asking me the same question twice like you're trying to trick me into changing my story. But my story doesn't change because it's the truth. I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. I know it in my bones, and I know it because I have the physical proof. 

I'm a logical guy, I work with my hands, I understand how the physical world operates. My tools don’t move themselves. They just don't! Gravity doesn't unhook a wrench from a pegboard and slide it under a heavy piece of machinery. And my fishing plans? They don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend. You don't have a perfectly maintained truck just magically drain its battery every Friday night, or find your expensive tackle box dumped out just in time to ruin a Saturday morning on the lake. That is a statistical impossibility. It takes human hands to do that. His hands. 

I've been watching this happen for a long time now. I've tracked the incidents. And after all these months, I can see it plain as day—he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. He wants me to sit here and second-guess myself, he wants you to ask me if I'm mistaken, he wants everyone to think I'm the one losing my grip so he can just slide right into my life. So no, doctor, there is no possibility I'm mistaken. The only mistake being made here is that nobody will just listen to the facts I'm laying right out on the table!
Was there anything unusual or stressful happening in your life before you started noticing these things with your tools and fishing plans?

Stressful? Unusual? Well, yeah, doc, I'd say having another grown man suddenly plop down in the middle of your living space is pretty unusual. I mean, if you want to talk about the exact timeline of when my life got turned upside down, we can talk about that. This whole nightmare, it has been going on for about nine months now. Nine months of this constant... this constant battle in my own home. 

And what else happened nine months ago? That is exactly when my wife’s relative moved into our house. 

Before that? Like I was telling you earlier, things were completely fine. We had our routine, my wife and I. It was quiet. Peaceful. I’d go to the plant, work my shift, come home, have dinner, maybe watch a little TV or head out to the garage to tinker with the outboard motor. Weekends were for the lake. But then, nine months ago, he supposedly needed a place to stay. You know how it goes, it was pitched to me as just a temporary thing. "He just needs to get back on his feet," she said. "It won't be long, just give him a little time." Well, here we are, three quarters of a year later, and he is still taking up space in the spare room. 

And that is exactly when all of this started. I mean, literally the exact same timeframe. It wasn't happening ten months ago. It wasn't happening a year ago. Nine months ago, he moves his boxes into my house, and suddenly my wrenches start walking away on their own. Suddenly my truck battery is draining itself dry on a Friday night. 

So, you want to talk about stress? You try living in your own home—the house where you pay the mortgage, you pay the electric bill, you put the food in the fridge—and you have this guy just... lurking around. Invading my space. Eyeing my things. So, yeah, if you want to point to a stressful event, that's it right there. Him moving in. That's the only thing that changed in my life. Nothing at the plant changed, my health didn't change, the truck didn't change. Just him crossing my threshold nine months ago. That's the start of it all.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt like someone was out to get you or plotting against you before your wife's relative moved in?

Doc, are you... are you pulling my leg here? Seriously, is this some kind of psychological test? Because I feel like I'm taking crazy pills, you literally just asked me this. I mean, ten minutes ago, we went over this exact same thing. Did you not write it down? Look at your notepad right there. I told you, no. Never. Not once. 

I have never in my fifty-four years on this earth had a period where I thought people were plotting against me. I'm not a... a conspiracy guy. I don't sit around looking over my shoulder. Look at my twenties, my thirties, my forties. I was working at the old stamping plant before I moved over to my current assembly job. I had a foreman back then, a guy named Rick. Absolute hardass. Always breathing down our necks about the daily quotas, always checking our stations. Now, a guy who thinks people are out to get him? He'd think Rick was targeting him specifically. But me? I just knew Rick was getting squeezed by upper management. I didn't take it personal. I never thought Rick was 'plotting' to get me fired or ruin my life. I just did my welds, clocked out, and went about my business. That is how I have lived my entire life. Just taking things at face value, dealing with what's right in front of me. 

So no, there was no 'period in my life' before this. None. Zero. It is just this one specific guy. And it really, really burns me up that I'm sitting here giving you the honest-to-God facts about what this relative is doing to my home, my sanctuary, and you keep trying to dig into my past like I've got some history of making up ghost stories. I don't. I never have. My record is completely clean on that front, doc, and you can ask anyone who's ever known me. You can ask my wife! Well, before she started taking his side and getting brainwashed by him, anyway. But she'd tell you, before nine months ago, I was always the most level-headed guy you'd ever meet. So can we please stop going backward and focus on what's actually happening right now?
Did you notice any changes in your thoughts, like hearing voices or seeing things that weren't there, before your wife's relative moved in?

Voices? Seeing things? Doc, come on. Are you listening to yourself? Now you're just straight up asking if I'm hallucinating? 

Look at me. I work as an assembler. I work with heavy machinery, presses, grinders, raw materials. You think a guy who hears voices that aren't there can survive decades on a fabrication floor? If you're seeing things that aren't there on the line, you lose a finger. You lose a hand. You get someone else killed. I rely on my eyes and my ears every single day to keep me alive and to do my job right. The only voices I hear are the guys on the floor yelling over the noise of the machines, or the foreman telling us the material shipment is running late. 

And before nine months ago? It was the exact same thing. My thoughts were fine. My hearing was fine. My eyesight was 20/20. I don't hear ghosts, doc. I don't see visions. I see what is physically, undeniably right in front of me. When I see my socket wrench sitting on the kitchen counter instead of in the locked red drawer of my toolbox out in the garage, that's not a hallucination. That is a physical, heavy metal object that was moved by a physical person. 

It just really feels like you're throwing everything at the wall here to see what sticks, trying to make me out to be some kind of loony tune. First you ask if I was paranoid before he moved in, now you're asking if I was hearing voices before he moved in. No! The answer is no. My thoughts are exactly the same as they were when I was twenty years old. Clear as a bell. I've never had a problem with my mind playing tricks on me, not before he moved in, not after. The only thing that has changed is that I've got this freeloader actively trying to sabotage my life, and now I've got a doctor trying to convince me my brain is broken instead of just looking at the very real, very physical evidence I'm trying to explain to you. So no, no voices, no visions, nothing like that. Just the reality of what this guy is doing to me.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or emotional state since you started noticing these things with your tools and fishing plans?

Mood? What do you mean by mood? Like, am I depressed or something? Because no, doc, I'm not depressed. I'm not having mood swings or crying in my beer or whatever it is you're looking for. 

I am exactly who I have always been. I'm a steady guy. Ask any of the guys at the plant, they'll tell you I'm the most even-keeled guy on the assembly line. But, I mean, if you're asking if I'm angry? Well, hell yes, I'm angry! But that's not a 'mood change,' doc, that's just... that's just common sense! That's a normal human reaction! 

Think about it. Just put yourself in my steel-toed boots for a single minute here. You wake up on a Saturday. You've been working your tail off all week, forty, maybe fifty hours on the floor, your back aches, your knees are clicking every time you take a step. All you want to do—the only thing you've been looking forward to—is to grab your gear, hitch up the boat, and get out on the water before the sun gets too high. It's your one day of peace. And then you walk out to the garage, and you find your favorite crankbaits—the ones you specifically organized by depth and color the night before—just dumped out and tangled up at the bottom of the box. Or you find out your fishing license, which you always, always keep in the exact same zippered side pocket of your duffel bag, is suddenly missing. 

How would that affect your mood? Would you be whistling a happy tune? Would you just smile and say, 'Oh well, guess I won't go fishing today'? No! You'd be seeing red! You'd be furious! Anyone would be! 

So yeah, I get mad when he messes with my stuff. I get frustrated. I get agitated when I try to explain to my wife that someone is tampering with my tools and she just rolls her eyes and tells me I'm misplacing things, when I know for an absolute, undeniable fact that I put my socket wrench in the locked red drawer. It's infuriating. It really is. It makes my blood boil to be treated like a fool in my own home. 

But it's not some kind of... chemical imbalance or whatever you doctors call it. It's not a mood problem. I don't need a happy pill. It's a 'there is a guy actively ruining my life and messing with my property' problem. If he packed his cardboard boxes tomorrow and got the hell out of my spare room, my 'mood' would be absolutely perfect. I'd be the happiest guy in the county. So no, my emotional state hasn't changed. My baseline is exactly the same as it was a year ago. The only thing that's changed is my tolerance for his garbage, which is completely gone.
Have you ever had any other thoughts or beliefs that you held strongly, but others did not agree with?

Other thoughts or beliefs? What, like... like the earth is flat or something? Or that the government is putting microchips in the water? Is that what you're getting at? 

Because no. Absolutely not. I'm a fabricator, doc. I work with steel and aluminum. You can't have 'strong beliefs' about a piece of 14-gauge sheet metal, okay? It either bends to the spec or it doesn't. It's math. It's physics. It's tangible. That's how my brain works. I've never been the guy at the bar arguing about crazy conspiracy theories or politics or whatever nonsense people get worked up about. I don't care about any of that. My beliefs are pretty standard, everyday stuff, you know? You work hard, you pay your bills, you take care of your property, you put your tools back where you found them. Ask any guy on my line, ask my neighbors, ask the guys I go fishing with. We all agree on that stuff. There's no disagreement there.

The only—and I mean the absolute *only*—thing that anyone has ever 'not agreed with' me on is what is happening right under my own roof right now. And honestly, it's really just my wife who doesn't agree! And she only doesn't agree because she's his blood, you know? She's got this... this massive blind spot for him. If it was some stranger off the street coming into our house and moving my socket wrenches and dumping out my crankbaits, she'd be calling the cops right alongside me. She'd be changing the locks. But because it's her relative, because she feels sorry for him or whatever, suddenly I'm the one who's got 'strong beliefs' that she doesn't agree with. 

But it's not a belief, doc! A belief is thinking the Lions are actually gonna make it to the Super Bowl this year. Knowing my tools were moved when I was the only one who had the key to the drawer, that is a fact. Knowing my fishing license didn't just walk out of my zippered duffel bag on its own, that is a fact. So no, I don't have any weird beliefs that people disagree with. I don't have a history of being some eccentric guy with wild ideas. I just have cold, hard facts that my wife refuses to look at because she doesn't want to admit her precious relative is a snake who's trying to push me to the breaking point. That's all it is. I just want my garage left alone and my things to stay where I put them. Is that really such a crazy belief to have?
Have you ever held a belief that you knew to be true, but others did not agree with, before your wife's relative moved in?

Before? Look, doc, I feel like we’re just going in circles here. I just told you this a few minutes ago. No. Nothing before. This whole situation, this entire nightmare that I’m living through, it has only been going on for about nine months. That’s it. Exactly nine months, ever since my wife’s relative moved into our home. 

Before that? My life was completely, one hundred percent normal. I didn't have any 'beliefs' that people disagreed with because there was absolutely nothing to disagree about! We just went to work, came home, maybe grilled some burgers on the back patio, watched the game, went fishing on the weekends. That was the routine. There was no drama. There was no arguing over where I left my tools because my tools were exactly where I left them.

But nine months ago... I remember it clear as day. We cleared out the spare room—the one my wife used to use for her sewing stuff that really just sat there collecting dust for years—and we brought his cardboard boxes in. And honestly, I was fine with it at first! I really was. I figured, hey, a guy's down on his luck, family helps family, right? You give a guy a hand up. I even helped him carry his mattress up the stairs. But that is exactly when it all started. Not ten years ago, not when I was a kid, not five years ago. Nine months. 

Before he dragged his bags up my concrete driveway nine months ago, my wife and I agreed on everything. My buddies at the plant agreed with me. Everything was just... fine. It was peaceful. So I don't know how many different ways I can explain the timeline to you, doc. I have never been a guy with weird beliefs or crazy ideas that people didn't believe. It is just these last nine months, ever since he unpacked his bags in my spare room and started actively messing with my life. That’s the start and the end of it.
Have you ever had a belief that you were completely certain of, but turned out to be incorrect?

Incorrect? Like... like I was just flat-out wrong about something big? I mean... look, if you're talking about, I don't know, thinking a bolt was a half-inch when it was really nine-sixteenths, sure, a guy makes a mistake in the shop every now and then. You grab the wrong wrench, you realize it, you fix it. But a belief? Something I was certain of, like what's happening right now? No. Never. 

Because I know exactly what you're getting at, doc. You're trying to see if maybe I'm just wrong about him. If maybe I'm just confused. But I'm not. I am only here, sitting in this chair right now, because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. My wife, she looks at me like I've got two heads when I bring it up, like I'm just making up fairy tales. But I know—I know in my gut and I know from the evidence—that my wife’s relative came into this house specifically to get at me. It was his plan from the very day I helped him carry that mattress up the stairs. 

I mean, you just have to look at it logically. My tools don’t move themselves! I don't care what anybody says, a heavy-duty torque wrench does not just sprout legs and migrate across the garage to hide under a pile of oily rags. And my fishing plans... it’s every weekend, doc. Every single weekend they get spoiled. I'll have the truck packed, the boat hitched, everything ready, and suddenly the trailer wiring is mysteriously chewed up, or my tackle box is dumped out, or my license is gone. You don't just have your plans ruined by accident that many times in a row. It defies the laws of probability. It’s deliberate. It's calculated. 

And after all these months of dealing with it, of watching him operate and seeing how he plays the victim whenever I call him out... I can see it plain as day. It all makes perfect sense. He’s been trying to take over my place. He wants to push me out. If he can make me look like I'm losing my marbles, if he can get my wife to think I'm the problem and send me off to doctors like you, then I'm gone, and he gets a free ride in my house. He gets the whole place to himself. 

So no, I'm not incorrect. I have never been more correct about anything in my entire fifty-four years on this earth. I'm just the only one who actually sees what's going on, and it's exhausting having to defend myself when the proof is sitting right there in my garage.
Have you ever had any other experiences where you believed someone was out to get you or plotting against you, besides what's been happening with your wife's relative?

No, no, no. See, this is exactly what I mean, doc. You're fishing for something that just isn't there. You want me to sit here and say, oh yeah, ten years ago I thought the mailman was spying on me, or I thought the cashier at the grocery store was poisoning my apples. But that never happened. None of that. 

I'm a regular guy. I’ve worked at the same fabrication plant for... what, twenty-two years now? You don't last twenty-two years on the floor if you're the kind of guy who thinks his foreman is out to get him, or if you think the guy running the press brake is secretly plotting against you. You just don't. I get along with everybody. Me and Dave, the guy who runs the CNC machine, we've been on the same bowling league on Thursday nights for a decade. I don't look at Dave and think he's trying to sabotage my average, you know? I don't look at my neighbor, Tom, who borrows my lawnmower every other week in the summer, and think he's trying to ruin my engine. It's ridiculous to even think about. 

My life was boring. Boring in a good way, a predictable way. The only plot I ever had to worry about was whether the walleye were gonna bite on a cloudy day or if I needed to switch to a different jig. That was the extent of it. I don't have a history of looking over my shoulder. I've never been a paranoid guy. I didn't even lock my truck doors when I was parked in my own driveway! Well, I didn't *used* to, anyway, before nine months ago. Now I have to lock everything, put padlocks on my tool chests, keep my keys on a carabiner hooked to my belt loop even when I'm just watching TV in my own living room. 

But before him? Never. If somebody had a problem with me in the past, we'd just hash it out like men. We'd talk it over, maybe yell a bit, and it was done. There was no sneaking around, no plotting, no psychological warfare. It is just him. It is *only* him. And I really need you to understand that, because if we keep digging around in my past looking for ghosts that aren't there, we're completely ignoring the guy who is currently, right this very second, probably out in my garage messing with my drill press while I'm stuck here talking to you.
Have you ever had a thought or belief that you held to be true, but later found out was not true?

Doc, are you... are you even listening to me? I feel like I'm talking to a brick wall here. You literally just asked me this exact same thing two minutes ago! You asked if I was incorrect, now you're asking if I found out something was 'not true.' It is the exact same question, just dressed up in different words. 

And my answer is exactly the same. No. Because, like I just got done explaining to you, I am only sitting in this office, in this chair, because everybody keeps acting like I’m just imagining all this. My wife, and now you, looking at me like I'm making up stories. But I haven't "found out it wasn't true" because it *is* true. I know—without a shadow of a doubt—that my wife’s relative came into this house specifically to get at me.
